Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're aiming to complete the Day‑Zero handoff and wire up the private deployment (VPC/on‑prem connector) during the 9/1‑9/2 maintenance window. To make sure we don't block the cutover, can you send the concrete day‑zero checklist and the exact network/account artifacts you need from us?

High‑level asks from our side:
- Confirm required firewall ports and destination ranges for your runtime.
- KMS / key wrapping guidance (we run AWS KMS in our account).
- Service account roles and example IAM policy that Redwood needs.
- Expected cert chain / TLS requirements and whether you require SAN entries.
- Any bastion/jumpbox public IP whitelisting.

I've attached our initial network diagram (helix_net_diag_v1.png) and a CSV with our currently allocated egress ranges (will follow with final ranges after change window is confirmed).

Can we block 30 minutes tomorrow for a brief handoff call with infra and SRE? Our availability: 11:00–12:30 or 15:00–16:30 PT.

Thanks,
Carlos Vega
Director, Platform Ops — Helix Health

Subject: Re: Private deployment: day‑zero env handoff & network wire‑up

Carlos — thanks for the diagram and the availability. 11:00 PT tomorrow works for us; I'll send a calendar invite after we confirm internal owners below.

I've attached our Day‑Zero wireup checklist (redwood_day0_wireup_checklist.pdf) — the contents are summarized inline so you can copy/paste into your runbook. Key prerequisites we need from Helix before we begin the activation window:

1) Account & IAM
- Tenant service account (preferred: AWS IAM role for cross‑account access) with the following minimal roles: S3 read for artifact fetch, KMS decrypt for wrapper key, CloudWatch putMetric if using hosted telemetry.
- Service account key rotation cadence noted in the checklist; provide principal ARN and contact.

2) Networking / Routing
- Public egress IP ranges to whitelist for interconnect (we need both user egress and control‑plane egress).
- BGP / peering details if using direct connect (ASN, BGP neighbors, MD5 if required).
- NAT behavior: is source NAT applied? We need predictable SNAT for telemetry and license checks.
- Firewall rules: allow outbound TCP 443 to our control plane endpoints and inbound TCP 22/443 only to bastion and management subnets — full list in the attached PDF.

3) TLS & Certs
- We support mutual TLS for service‑to‑service connections. If you want mTLS, provide cert issuer and CSR pipeline. Public CA cert chain is fine; SAN must include the assigned hostname we provide.

4) KMS / Keywrap
- If using AWS KMS, create a key policy allowing the Redwood service principal (we include the example in the checklist). For customer‑managed keys we will request a Grant during provisioning.

5) Access & Jumpbox
- Bastion public IP(s) for SSH whitelisting and jumpbox user(s. If you prefer a temporary pre‑shared key for tunnel setup, provide details via secure channel.

6) Telemetry & Logging
- Acceptable syslog endpoint or S3 bucket for logs. If using S3, please ensure the bucket policy allows our read prefix.

7) Verification & Smoke
- We will run a set of smoke tests (connectivity, token exchange, sample inference) during Day‑Zero; please designate an on‑call SRE to validate the results.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood network owner: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwoodinference.com) — overall wireup coordination
- Redwood infra owner: Kimberly Park (kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com) — service account & certs
- Helix on‑call SRE: Carlos Vega / ops team — provide IP ranges and approve smoke tests

Next steps:
- Carlos: share final egress ranges and preferred authentication for KMS by EOD 8/23.
- Kimberly: I'll attach a service account template and expected IAM policy in a follow up.
- Marissa: prepping the day‑zero runbook and smoke test checklist, will link to Drive.

I attached the PDF checklist and added a Drive link with the runbook templates: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-day0-wireup

Thanks — we'll aim to lock details today so ops can schedule the maintenance window cleanly.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben / team — quick clarifications from the infra side:

- Service account template: attaching 'service-account-template.yaml' for Helix to populate. We require the following fields: principal_arn, allowed_ips (CIDR list), grant_token_contact.
- Egress expectations: we need deterministic SNAT so our telemetry and token validation see a stable source IP. Carlos — please confirm whether your egress IPs are stable during the maintenance window or if they can move (NAT pool changes).
- Firewall ports (abbreviated):
   * Outbound TCP 443 to control.redwoodinference.com (443)
   * Outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwoodinference.com (443)
   * Inbound TCP 22 to bastion IPs only (SSH)
   * Inbound TCP 8443 to management plane (if you enable it)

- VPN/pre‑shared key: if you're using site‑to‑site VPN as a backup, please provide PSK over secure channel and confirm lifetime.

Ben — I can own the service account validation and cert CSR exchange during Day‑Zero. Marissa — can you add the smoke test checklist to the Drive folder and include expected pass criteria?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
